The Tampa Bay Rays aren’t ready to call it a season. With their World Series hopes hanging by a thread, Tampa Bay delivered a thrilling 4-3 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers in 12 innings Tuesday night, keeping its championship dreams alive and forcing a fifth game.

Facing elimination after dropping the first three games of the series, the Rays entered Game 4 knowing there was no room for another defeat. Milwaukee, meanwhile, was looking to complete a sweep and celebrate the first World Series championship in franchise history.

For much of the night, neither team could gain a decisive advantage. The game remained tied at 2-2 through nine innings, with both pitching staffs keeping opposing hitters in check as the tension continued to build.

The Brewers appeared to have delivered the decisive blow in the top of the 12th inning when rookie Cooper Pratt launched a solo home run off Tampa Bay pitcher Ian Seymour. The blast gave Milwaukee a 3-2 lead and moved the Brewers closer to securing the championship.

But Tampa Bay had other plans.

The Rays opened the bottom of the 12th with an opportunity created by a throwing error from Milwaukee third baseman Joey Ortiz, allowing Junior Caminero to reach base. Liam Hicks followed with a single, setting the stage for a remarkable comeback.

Jonny DeLuca then delivered a clutch single to center field, bringing home pinch-runner Cedric Mullins and tying the game at 3-3.

With momentum shifting toward the home team, Chandler Simpson added another single to load the bases. Milwaukee responded by positioning five infielders in an attempt to prevent the winning run from scoring.

That strategy couldn’t stop Ben Williamson.

The Tampa Bay pinch-hitter, who had struggled offensively throughout the postseason, connected on a ground ball that cleared first baseman Jake Bauers and reached right field. The hit brought home the winning run and sent Tropicana Field into celebration.

The victory was especially significant considering the historical challenge facing Tampa Bay. Only five teams have managed to win Game 4 of the World Series after falling behind 3-0, and none of the previous four went on to win Game 5.

The Rays now have an opportunity to challenge that history, although the road ahead remains difficult.

The only team in Major League Baseball history to overcome a 3-0 deficit in any best-of-seven postseason series was the 2004 Boston Red Sox, who accomplished the feat against the New York Yankees in the American League Championship Series.

For Milwaukee, the loss represents a missed opportunity rather than the end of its championship pursuit. The Brewers still control the series with a 3-1 advantage and need just one more victory to secure their first title.

Tampa Bay, however, has demonstrated that it won’t surrender without a fight.

Game 5 is scheduled for Wednesday night at Tropicana Field, where the Rays will attempt to extend the series once again.

Milwaukee remains firmly in control of the championship race, but Tampa Bay has ensured that the World Series will continue for at least one more night.

Eddie Vedder and Stephen Wilson Jr. have brought a Seattle rock classic back into the spotlight with the official release of their live performance of “Hunger Strike,” recorded at the 2026 Ohana Festival in Dana Point, California.

The collaboration took place in September when Vedder made an unexpected appearance during Wilson Jr.’s festival set. The Pearl Jam frontman had performed with Eddie Vedder and Friends on the festival’s opening night but returned the following evening to join the rising country-rock artist for a song with deep roots in his musical history.

Their performance revisited the 1991 Temple of the Dog single that originally paired Vedder with Soundgarden frontman Chris Cornell. The newly released professional video captures the two singers sharing the stage, bringing renewed attention to one of the most recognizable songs from Seattle’s early 1990s rock movement.

For Wilson Jr., the opportunity represented a memorable collaboration with one of the artists connected to the song’s original recording. His reaction at the conclusion of the performance reflected the excitement of the moment.

“Hunger Strike” holds a special place in rock history. The song appeared on Temple of the Dog’s self-titled album, which grew out of Cornell’s desire to honor his friend and former roommate Andrew Wood, the Mother Love Bone singer who died in 1990.

The project united Cornell with musicians who would become central figures in Pearl Jam, including Stone Gossard, Jeff Ament and Mike McCready, alongside Soundgarden drummer Matt Cameron. What began as a smaller tribute recording developed into a full-length album that connected several important figures in Seattle’s emerging rock community.

Vedder’s original vocal contribution helped make “Hunger Strike” one of the project’s signature recordings. More than three decades later, his appearance alongside Wilson Jr. offers a new interpretation of the song while maintaining its connection to the musicians and friendships behind its creation.

The collaboration also highlights Wilson Jr.’s ability to move between musical styles. His combination of country songwriting and rock influences makes the Temple of the Dog material a natural meeting point between his musical approach and Vedder’s alternative rock background.

With the official performance video now available, the Ohana Festival moment reaches audiences beyond those who attended the September event.

Meanwhile, Wilson Jr. continues an international touring schedule that includes European performances followed by additional U.S. dates in November and December. His year-end itinerary includes a New Year’s Eve appearance at Choctaw Casino & Resort in Durant, Oklahoma.

For longtime Temple of the Dog fans, the collaboration offers another opportunity to revisit a landmark recording. For listeners discovering Wilson Jr., it provides an introduction to his rock influences through a song that remains closely associated with Vedder and Cornell’s musical legacy.

Kim Kardashian is reflecting on one of the most emotional moments of her life, recalling the final conversations she shared with her father, Robert Kardashian Sr., before his death more than two decades ago.

The television personality and businesswoman was only 22 years old when her father died of esophageal cancer in September 2003. Although her life has changed dramatically since then, the guidance he offered during his final days remains an important part of her story.

Robert, a prominent Los Angeles attorney, wanted his daughter to feel confident about her future. He also encouraged her to look after her siblings, leaving her with a responsibility that extended beyond their final goodbye.

For Kardashian, those memories represent more than a painful family loss. They are reminders of the close relationship she shared with her father and the values he hoped his children would carry forward.

Over the years, Kardashian has frequently spoken about Robert’s influence on her life. His career in law became particularly meaningful as she began pursuing legal studies and developing an interest in criminal justice reform.

While millions know Kardashian for her reality television career, business ventures and influence in fashion and beauty, her ambitions have expanded well beyond entertainment.

Her decision to pursue legal education has also created a personal connection to her father’s professional legacy. She has previously expressed how meaningful it would have been to discuss her studies with him and receive his encouragement firsthand.

The loss has taken on different dimensions as Kardashian has grown older and become a mother herself. Her father never had the opportunity to watch her children grow up or witness the many milestones that followed his death.

Still, Kardashian has continued to celebrate his memory through family photographs, personal stories and reflections on their relationship.

Her latest recollections offer a more personal perspective on a celebrity whose public life is often dominated by headlines about business, relationships and television.

Behind that highly visible career is a daughter who continues to carry her father’s words with her.

More than two decades after his passing, Robert Kardashian’s influence remains part of Kim’s journey, demonstrating how a parent’s love and encouragement can continue shaping a family across generations.
